acceptance.given: Stable and Candidate subjects are selected for Matrix execution with repository-relative identities under the frozen SM-6 requirement.

oracle.expected: Eligibility verification passes only when Stable has independently verifiable provenance for existing supported behavior and Candidate contains the real change under evaluation; the eligibility record binds both identities before matrix execution.
forbidden: Stable is accepted without verifiable provenance for existing supported behavior.
Candidate is accepted without containing the real change under evaluation.
oracle.observable: A machine-readable eligibility receipt records Stable provenance verification, Candidate change-content verification, both immutable identities, and a pass/fail eligibility verdict before matrix execution.

acceptance.then: Before any Matrix Case starts, the toolchain verifies and records the Stable provenance and Candidate evaluated-change bindings; only a passing receipt permits matrix execution.
acceptance.when: Stable and Candidate subjects are selected for Matrix execution.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the eligibility validator against a Stable subject whose provenance reference or existing-behavior support binding is absent or unverifiable; assert Stable eligibility is rejected before matrix execution.

Run the eligibility validator against a Candidate subject that lacks the real change under evaluation while all other inputs remain valid; assert Candidate eligibility is rejected before matrix execution.

affected_subjects: Stable eligibility provenance and immutable identity
Candidate evaluated-change presence and immutable identity
slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or repair the Toolchain replay eligibility gate so Stable provenance for existing supported behavior and Candidate inclusion of the actual evaluated change are independently verified and recorded before any Matrix Case execution; missing or unverifiable bindings fail closed.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay and matrix receipt formats and fail-closed behavior; eligibility rejection prevents matrix execution without mutating Stable, Candidate, historical, or authorization state.

slice_hint.state_transition: Unverified Stable/Candidate selection -> independently verified eligibility receipt -> matrix execution allowed; any missing, unverifiable, or mismatched provenance/change binding -> terminal eligibility failure and no matrix execution.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Eligible iff Stable provenance is verifiable for existing supported behavior, Candidate contains the real evaluated change, both identities are immutable and repository-bound, and the eligibility receipt is bound before matrix execution; otherwise terminal failure.

acceptance.given: Pinned inputs and their coverage result are available for evaluation from a fresh checkout.

oracle.expected: The fresh-checkout evaluation produces the same coverage result as the pinned-input evaluation.
forbidden: A coverage result that differs from the result produced from the pinned inputs.
oracle.observable: The S24 test evidence records pinned-input and fresh-checkout coverage results with a machine-verifiable equality comparison.

acceptance.then: Reproducibility is accepted only when fresh-checkout coverage equals the pinned-input coverage result.
acceptance.when: Evaluate the pinned inputs in a fresh checkout and compare the resulting coverage to the pinned-input result.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the fresh-checkout pinned-input evaluation and fail when its coverage result differs from the pinned-input coverage result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Evaluate pinned inputs from a fresh checkout and emit a machine-verifiable coverage equality comparison.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve pinned-input evaluation semantics and mark prior evidence stale when bound inputs differ.

slice_hint.state_transition: Coverage evaluation transitions from pinned-input result to fresh-checkout reproduction or mismatch failure.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Reproduction succeeds only when fresh-checkout coverage equals pinned-input coverage under unchanged bound inputs; mismatch fails closed.

acceptance.given: A fresh checkout and pinned Current Snapshot are available, including the historical evidence and all result-determining input identities.

oracle.expected: The verifier reconstructs the exact original identities without rewriting historical evidence, then launches a new process replay bound to those same identities and records attributable replay evidence.
forbidden: A claimed replay without a fresh process execution
oracle.observable: The identity-reconstruction check and fresh replay output show the same bound identities and an attributable new process execution.

acceptance.then: A fresh replay executes against the exact reconstructed pinned inputs.
acceptance.when: After the planned source-identity selector is authored, the snapshot reconstruction and replay selector is executed from the fresh checkout.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Mutate or substitute one reconstructed bound identity and verify that replay fails closed rather than running under a different identity.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reconstruct the original binding identity from the pinned snapshot, verify historical evidence without rewriting it, and run the fresh replay using that same identity.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Historical evidence remains immutable; identity mismatch invalidates replay rather than altering prior records.

slice_hint.state_transition: Pinned snapshot identities reconstructed -> same-identity fresh replay executed with attributable evidence.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The original binding is reconstructed, the replay uses the same identity, identity mismatch is rejected, historical evidence is unchanged, and a fresh process replay is attributable to the pinned identities.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain-only TC-D1 semantic-change proposal is evaluated against the governed Skill-input v2 contract and the explicit non-goal forbidding redesign of Skill-input v1/current-pointer semantics.

oracle.expected: The validation artifact records rejection of any v1/current-pointer semantic redesign and confirms that existing Skill-input v2 behavior remains the governed contract.
forbidden: The proposal is accepted while redesigning Skill-input v1/current-pointer semantics.
Skill-input v2 behavior is replaced, weakened, or reinterpreted by the change.
A Phase service, runtime, Hosted workspace, or installed BMAD/GDS path is used as the implementation owner.
oracle.observable: A deterministic Toolchain validator/test receipt contains a rejected protocol-redesign result, identifies the unchanged v2 contract, and binds the result to the inspected proposal and source requirement.

acceptance.then: When a proposed Skill-input semantic change is submitted within TC-D1 work, run the bounded Toolchain governance check before any implementation acceptance or publication.
acceptance.when: A Skill-input semantic change is proposed within TC-D1 work.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A proposal that redesigns Skill-input v1/current-pointer semantics is presented without an independently observable rejection and v2-preservation check.
The check resolves a Phase service, runtime, Hosted workspace, or installed BMAD/GDS path instead of the Toolchain governance owner.

affected_subjects: Skill-input v1/current-pointer semantic redesign proposals and the governed Skill-input v2 contract
slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or maintain a Toolchain governance assertion that rejects redesign of Skill-input v1/current-pointer semantics, explicitly preserves current Skill-input v2 behavior, and emits a deterministic rejection/preservation receipt; it must not alter v2 implementation semantics.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert only the added governance assertion/receipt wiring; preserve the existing Skill-input v2 schema, generation/current-pointer data, and all existing replay consumers.

slice_hint.state_transition: proposal received -> Toolchain governance check evaluates v1/current-pointer boundary -> redesign rejected and v2 contract remains active; missing or ambiguous evidence fails closed.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Terminal success requires an independently bound rejection of the v1/current-pointer redesign plus confirmation that Skill-input v2 remains unchanged and governed; otherwise the result is unsuccessful.
